requirements.evidence: Migration matches the schema, including unique (entity_id,email), cascade and a nullable invited_by (migration:14-24). The email mutator lowercases and trims (EntityInvite.php:40-45). sendInvite (Members.php:52-117) has the specified validation, member and pending checks, delete-then-recreate for expired or accepted invites, a UniqueConstraintViolationException catch that becomes an inviteEmail error, a RateLimiter hit only after success, a queued mail, an audit log and a form reset. PendingInvites::accept is idempotent, records expired as an error on 'invite', uses firstOrCreate for the membership, sets the session and redirects. The <hr> only renders when invites exist (pending-invites.blade.php:4-7). The modal header is ui.members_details and the role select has no empty option. confirmRemoval/cancelRemoval/removeMember reset state. Mount uses authorize('update'). en/pt_BR strings are present.

conventions.evidence: Docs are updated (business-rules.md, database-schema.md, CHANGELOG) and authorization goes through policies. Invite creation (Members.php:83), invite deletion and membership creation on accept (PendingInvites.php:53) are inline Eloquent writes in Livewire components, not app/Actions classes. Rules are passed inline to $this->validate([...]) and the #[Validate] import was removed (Members.php:56-59), instead of the project's #[Validate] pattern. The CHANGELOG entry is also copied into the released [0.0.0] section.

security.evidence: Every Members action calls authorize, and params are resolved through $this->entity->memberships()/invites() (findOrFail scoped to the entity). PendingInvites checks the invitee on every call (inviteForCurrentUser) and also requires a verified e-mail. Accept locks the row with lockForUpdate. The separator is #[Locked]. Blade output is all {{ }}. $fillable is declared. selectedMembershipId is client-writable and not #[Locked], but saveRole re-resolves it through the entity scope and the assignRole policy, and a tamper test covers it, so the impact is limited.

tests.evidence: EntityInviteTest.php covers the schema and unique constraint, cascade/nullOnDelete, the factory, mutator write paths, mail rendering in both locales, accept/decline/idempotency/expired/duplicate membership, a non-invitee 403, an unverified account, and onboarding with and without the hr. MembersTest covers employee 403 (route and component), validation datasets including owner, the race test, the rate limit with invalid input not consuming quota, the error rendering exactly once, foreign invite/membership tamper tests, saveRole rules, and the removal modal.

simplicity.evidence: Manager counting is extracted into managerCount() (Members.php:226), which removes the existing duplication. The dashboard view is simplified to a single @if ($isManager && Route::has(...)). Minor extras: closeMember(), inviter() relation and isPending() are not strictly required.

readability.evidence: Methods are small and named clearly, with short comments that explain intent (e.g. 'Lost a race against a concurrent invite'). Views use wire:key and accessible labels. sendInvite is somewhat long (~65 lines) and mixes several concerns that an Action would separate.

scope.evidence: Nearly everything serves the task. The navbar switcher link now also appears when there are pending invites (default-page.blade.php:69), which is a reasonable supporting change. The CHANGELOG duplicate under the released 0.0.0 section is an unrelated and incorrect edit.

issues.explanation: Domain writes (creating invites, accepting into a membership) are done inline in Livewire components instead of through app/Actions classes as the conventions require.
Validation rules are passed inline to $this->validate([...]) and the #[Validate] attribute pattern was dropped, deviating from the project's Livewire validation convention.
The new 'Added' entry is duplicated into the already released [0.0.0] section, which falsifies release history.
selectedMembershipId is server-selected context but is not #[Locked]; it is safely re-resolved in saveRole, but locking it would match the Livewire policy.
Accept/decline also require a verified e-mail, which the task does not specify; the extra check is defensible but stricter than the specification.

review.summary: The change replaces direct member adding with an invite flow: migration, model, factory, a queued markdown mail, sendInvite/cancelInvite, the PendingInvites component, a manager-only members page with a detail modal and a removal confirmation modal, docs, translations and thorough tests including tamper and authorization cases. The requirements are met and the security is solid. The remaining deviations are conventions: writes are not in Actions, the #[Validate] pattern is not used, and the CHANGELOG entry is duplicated into a released section. So I would approve after small fixes.
